title: Exercise therapy for a child's scoliosis
what: These are special exercises that strengthen the back muscles and teach your child to hold good posture. They are chosen to fit the type of curve.
why: For children and teens with scoliosis or poor posture, on their own or together with a brace.
duration: a session usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; exercising continues for months
tell_doctor: What the X-rays showed and what the orthopedist said
Whether your child wears a brace
What your child does: sports, dance

prepare.title: X-rays
prepare.text: Bring the X-ray and the orthopedist's report. The instructor chooses exercises from them.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Close-fitting sports clothes so the back can be seen. Barefoot or in socks is fine.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Your child should not eat a heavy meal in the hour before.

steps: The instructor examines your child's back and posture
Explains to your child how their scoliosis works
Teaches special breathing and correct body position
Does the exercises in front of a mirror
Shows you, the parent, how to practice at home
Regularly checks how your child does the exercises
feel: Muscles may tire and ache a little
Children sometimes get bored. Games and praise help
after: Practice at home every day, preferably at the same time
Watch posture at the desk and on the phone
See the orthopedist regularly and have X-rays when advised
red_flags: Numbness or weakness in the legs: see a doctor

faq.a: It helps stop the curve from getting worse and improves posture. How much depends on the degree.

faq.q: Can my child just go swimming?
faq.a: Swimming is good, but it does not replace the special exercises.

reminders.text: Your child's exercise therapy is today. Bring sports clothes, water and the X-rays.
